items.description: R1 (#625): "NodeMemoryStalled (critical) and NodeMemoryStallElevated (warning) have both been firing on srvk8s3 since ~2026-08-13, across 485 five-minute buckets." / "Alertmanager still has no receiver configured, so none of it was sent anywhere." / "Two coupled facets: the alert rules trust a counter that can wedge, and there is no delivery path to notice when they misfire — or when they fire for real." Both facets are closed on production: the two stall alerts no longer fire on a wedged counter alone (today they read the stall rate and nothing else — HelmCharts configs/prd/prometheus/prd/values.yaml:75-90), and Alertmanager, on the chart's stock receiver with no configuration today (values.yaml:120-130 sets none), delivers alerts to Telegram.

items.area: R2 — Grafana and pgAdmin on Keycloak (#575)
items.description: R2 (#575): "Put Grafana and pgAdmin behind the homelab Keycloak (`homelab` realm at https://auth.ginbov.nl/realms/homelab) instead of their app-local logins, same shape as dnsmasq / electronics-inventory / iot / guacamole / open-webui / zigbee2mqtt already use" — per-app confidential client, secret in OpenBao at eso/<cluster>/<app>/<stage>/oidc, materialised by ESO, OIDC config in the chart/release values (the dnsmasq shape: HelmCharts configs/prd/dnsmasq/prd/values.yaml:19-51). Holds on both clusters, the dev-cluster copies against the dev Keycloak's homelab-dev realm; no client secret appears in any committed file.

R3: "a Keycloak upgrade would be warrented" — Keycloak is built at 26.7.3 in DockerImages (26.5.1 today, keycloak/build-matrix.json:5) and every charts/keycloak release runs it (HelmCharts charts/keycloak/values.yaml:22 pins 26.5.1 today), with a backup of Keycloak's database taken before the push that deploys it.

Each stall alert fires only when available memory is low or major faults are high as well: NodeMemoryStalled and NodeMemoryStallElevated additionally require, on the same node, MemAvailable under 10% of MemTotal or major page faults above 500/s, with their stall thresholds (0.05 / 0.02), severities and for-windows otherwise unchanged (HelmCharts configs/prd/prometheus/prd/values.yaml:75-97 today). The 2026-08-02 incident meets both signals (0.62 GiB MemAvailable, 670–770 major faults/s — AnsibleSpecs handovers/memory-issues/06-eviction.md:73, 02-measurements.md:136).

A new warning-level alert fires when a node's memory stall rate is above 0.02 while MemAvailable is above 25% of MemTotal and major faults average under 50/s over an hour, held for at least an hour; its message names the node and says the stall alerts on that node are blind until it is rebooted.

The production alerting rules load and evaluate without errors, including while a node-exporter chart upgrade leaves overlapping series per node, and none of the node-memory-pressure alerts fires on production's nodes as they stand after deploy.

Production Alertmanager delivers to the chat of a new, dedicated Telegram bot (neither eso/prd/jenkins-telegram-bot nor eso/prd/telegram-mcp is reused): critical alerts delivered loud, warning alerts delivered silent, resolved notices sent, plain text. The bot token and chat id come from OpenBao eso/prd/prometheus/prd/telegram via ESO and appear in neither git nor the rendered Alertmanager configuration.

Delivery covers the production cluster's Alertmanager only: the dev cluster's Prometheus release is unchanged, no SMTP gateway or mail-derived event receivers are added, and Alertmanager gains no ingress.

On both clusters, an account holding the grafana Keycloak client's admin role signs in to Grafana through Keycloak as Grafana Admin, and a realm account without that role — F1's friend — cannot log in.

On both clusters, an account holding the pgadmin Keycloak client's admin role signs in to pgAdmin through Keycloak as a pgAdmin administrator that already lists and can connect to the chart's postgres-pas server (HelmCharts charts/pgadmin/files/servers.json), and a realm account without that role cannot log in.
Grafana and pgAdmin each keep their local admin and login form as break-glass; Keycloak is an additional login button, with no automatic redirect.

The rollout that deploys Keycloak 26.7.3 never runs a 26.5.1 and a 26.7.3 pod against the same database at once (Keycloak upgrading guide, "Migrating to 26.6.0"; the chart surges a second pod today — HelmCharts charts/keycloak/templates/keycloak-deployment.yaml:10-14), and keycloak-dev.home runs 26.7.3 healthily before auth.ginbov.nl does.
After the upgrade, the homelab and homelab-dev login pages render with the deployed themes, and a sign-in through an app already on Keycloak succeeds on each realm.
